title: Review of c43's CIPS consumer on fresh seed 17: X replicates against a matched twin; consumers are short-lived bands on prey edges (median life 400 t, 39% born by nucleation), D only at K=5
summary: Re-ran world.py (defaults, 128^2, t=12000, --lineage-k 5) on fresh seed 17 with its matched consumer-free twin. X replicates: the twin is a frozen emulsion (75 prey, 5 persistent splits, 0 moving tracks) while with consumers prey divide (76 persistent splits, generation 7) and move (95 moving tracks), at about half the prey number (39 vs 75). Consumers look as in the claim: rod-shaped bands on prey edges. By labkit's own tracking of the consumer channel, 693 tracks for about 30 bodies, median life 400 t (p90 1000 t, 10 tracks of 2000 t or more), 267 of 693 born by nucleation; 19 persistent splits at K=5 (generation 2) and 0 at the default K=20; 42% of consumer mass lies inside prey (c_a > 0.5).

observations.S: rerun/seed17/sheet.png t=0: unstructured over the whole domain
observations.X: twin_seed17/FACTS.md vs rerun/seed17/FACTS.md: prey persistent splits 5 vs 76, moving tracks 0 vs 95, final prey 75 vs 39; sign on prey: fewer but dividing and moving bodies; consumers need prey per the claim's efork (not re-run)
observations.I: consumer_tracks_seed17.json: median consumer track 400 t, 1.4% of tracks last 2000 t, 39% of births are nucleations from the bath; bands on prey edges (sheet.png), 42% of consumer mass inside prey: not shown to be persistent individuals rather than a self-made layer on prey
observations.D: consumer_tracks_seed17.json: 19 persistent splits (gen 2) at K=5, 0 at labkit's default K=20; rerun/seed17/FACTS.md labkit persistent consumer tracks 0

seeds_run.result: X and S reproduce; I and D do not meet their gates

controls_run.X: twin_seed17 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration, K=5)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed at 128^2; E fork not re-run. I and D are counted as not seen here (in 'observations' for the record, not in 'supported').
